chapter: Chick Webb, Lucky Roberts, Alex Jackson
title: Lucky Roberts and society jobs for the rich
summary: Scott plays dates with Roberts for wealthy patrons, on Cecil Smith's advice.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So Lucky Roberts, he called me up and asked me, could I play some dates with him. Well, I'd heard of him. Lucky played for strictly rich people. Well, I had played for rich people on Fifth Avenue, because nothing but rich people used to live there. I played for rich people. But he had rich people out in Westbury and around there, and around Southampton, where the rich people used to be living at one time. Not now, but then. Nothing but rich people -- the Goulds, the Vanderbilts, the Astors, the Rockefellers and all the rich people.

Well, he asked me, did I have any open dates? I told him I'd look and see. I was working at the time, but he said, I'd like to have you play with me, Scottie, let me know. So I went to my good old friend -- Cecil Smith wasn't playing then, he wasn't playing, he'd given it up. He was keeping a bar near the Amsterdam.

And he was the one that advised me to go with Fletcher. And I listened to him because he was older and more experienced than me, and he knew more about Lucky Roberts than I did. So I told him about it, and he said, well, I'll tell you like I told you about Fletcher. He says, there's good money in it, those rich people pay good money. Said, if Lucky

called you and he's got an open gig, take it. The only thing is, he doesn't pay you right away, because those rich people, they pay by check. Like the other places, you get your money when you get through. No.

Well, I didn't mind that because I was working and I had a little money myself. He said, well, when you get an open date, then call. So I called him. Lucky, he says, oh, I'm glad, Scottie, you're just in time. And he gave me a gig. And it was for rich people, out there in Westbury.
This is after you left Chick Webb?
What year? Do you remember what year?
